mainEntity.name: Is the explainer a simulation of a real ultrasound machine?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. It is a conceptual animation of the pulse-echo mechanism, built from a mechanism brief that links to a National Academies/NCBI reference on diagnostic imaging. It does not model any specific device, and nothing in it should be read as a performance claim.

mainEntity.name: Why is every frame a pure function of its index?

acceptedAnswer.text: So the browser player and the rendered MP4 are identical by construction. If animation state accumulated over time, the two outputs could drift apart. With a pure draw function, frame 300 is frame 300 everywhere, which also makes review and bug reports precise.

Cyan #00E5FF is the acoustic path (the pulse out and the echo back). Gold #FFD166 is energy or actuation (the electrical excitation of an element). Violet #9D4EDD is measurement or state (received signal, timing, image data). The stage is #0B1019. Color is explanatory, not literal emission.

mainEntity.name: Why does the depth formula say sound speed is assumed?

acceptedAnswer.text: Because d = c·t/2 converts a measured arrival time into a depth using a value of c that the machine does not measure. The soft-tissue imaging convention is approximately 1540 m/s. Where real tissue differs from that value, the reported depth differs from the true depth. The label keeps that assumption visible.

mainEntity.name: Can my team reuse this in training or sales material?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, as a description of the mechanism. Do not overlay device specifications, performance figures, or clinical claims on it. The explainer is deliberately free of those, and adding them would turn a conceptual animation into an unsupported product claim.
